overview: Underwriting Submission Appetite Screening addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in insurance operations. The first proof of value uses broker submissions, risk schedules and underwriting rules. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is submission-to-quote lead time, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: broker submissions, risk schedules and underwriting rules; define submission-to-quote lead time and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Chief Claims Officer / Chief Underwriter.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
